steps.title: See it
steps.text: This is the elephant of xiangqi, Chinese chess. (Shako and janggi have elephants that move differently; they have their own lessons.) It moves exactly two squares diagonally, and takes the same way, but it doesn't jump: if the square in between is taken, it can't go that way. In xiangqi it may never cross the river in the middle of the board, so it stays on its own half. This app has no river, so here it may go anywhere. The marked squares are every square it can reach.

steps.title: Try it
steps.text: Move the elephant to the marked square. Your own pawn on e5 is in the way, so go around it: it takes three moves.

pages.text: The elephant is a weak piece, worth about a pawn. Like the alfil, it can only ever reach eight squares of the board, and it can also be blocked. Here the pawn on e5 stands between it and f6, so it can't go there.
The elephant is a defender. Keep it near your king, where its few squares are the ones that matter. Two elephants can guard each other, like these on c1 and e3.
Moving a piece out of the way opens the elephant's path. Here your knight on e5 blocks the way to f6. Move the knight, and the elephant attacks the black rook.

puzzles.hint: Two squares diagonally, and the square in between is empty.

puzzles.prompt: Win the black pawn in two moves.
puzzles.hint: The pawn can't move, as your knight blocks it. Move the elephant to a square from which it attacks the pawn.
Your king already takes the king's squares away. Check it with the elephant across b2, which is empty.
An elephant on f3 would check the king, but only if g2 is empty. Clear the way first.
